statement: Summation is the addition of a sequence of numbers (called addends or summands) or, more generally, elements of any mathematical type on which an operation denoted '+' is defined (such as functions, vectors, matrices, or polynomials), resulting in their sum or total denoted by the capital sigma notation \sum.

symbols.meaning: summation operator denoting repeated addition over an indexed sequence
the summand or addend evaluated at index n
symbols.dimensions: element of a set with an addition operation '+'

symbols.meaning: lower bound of the summation index
upper bound of the summation index

properties.why: the sum from the first term up to the last is equal to the sum from the last down to the first
commutativity and associativity of addition permit interchanging the order of summation

properties.property: \sum_{k \leq j \leq i \leq n} a_{i,j} = \sum_{i=k}^n \sum_{j=k}^i a_{i,j} = \sum_{j=k}^n \sum_{i=j}^n a_{i,j} = \sum_{j=0}^{n-k} \sum_{i=k}^{n-j} a_{i+j,i}
properties.why: commutativity and associativity applied over triangular index domains
splitting a sum into its even and odd indexed parts
the logarithm of a product is the sum of the logarithms of the factors
the exponential of a sum is the product of the exponentials of the summands
the term c does not depend on the summation index i
sum of the simplest arithmetic progression consisting of the first n natural numbers
sum of a geometric progression when the common ratio a is different from 1

assumptions.assumption: The summands belong to a domain equipped with an operation denoted '+'
assumptions.breaks_when: The terms belong to a set or type without an addition operation defined

assumptions.assumption: The sequence being summed is finite
assumptions.breaks_when: The sequence has infinitely many terms, becoming a series requiring limits

assumptions.assumption: In geometric progression evaluations, the common ratio a is not equal to 1
assumptions.breaks_when: a = 1, which causes a division-by-zero failure in the formula (1 - a^n)/(1 - a)

failure_modes.mode: Division by zero in geometric progression sum
failure_modes.cause: Evaluating \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} a^i via the closed-form formula when a = 1
Attempting to sum elements from a structure on which addition '+' is not defined

failure_modes.signature: Sum does not resolve to a well-defined finite total
failure_modes.cause: Applying finite summation rules to an infinite sequence without using limits
